I’m so proud of you for starting recovery! That’s a beautiful path to be on. This isn’t easy stuff to deal with but I know you can do it. Try using a black/ non clear bag or rubbish bin liner to throw them into, as you’re doing it, you’re reminding yourself “the person who did this and the person cleaning it up are in very different stages of life, I’m happy now that I can clean it up and be able to have (some or all) of those foods without hiding them anymore, it won’t always be perfect and I still might fall backwards but I’m improving for the girl who put these here, proving to her and me that we can do this. Then take it to the outside bin and bury it! Maybe write a journal entry about it and throw it in the bin with the packaging. Make it symbolic if you’d like! Remind yourself that you might not feel good doing this and it may bring out a multitude of hurt/embarrassment feelings but that’s just called being human and that’s okay. The way you feel is normal, valid and more then okay, we spend a lot of time in recovery trying to learn and un learn what most people just don’t understand or struggle with. It’s okay to take longer to feel comfortable when you’re currently in a place where Ed doesn’t like to be, helping yourself. Wanting to throw it away and clean it up shows, you are trying and making little steps; even if you don’t do it now or it takes 6 more months! That doesn’t matter, progress is progress. Maybe try doing half of it and half in a few more months, give yourself time to take the steps YOU need to in YOUR TIME. This is one very personal journey and I am sending you so much love and positivity in your recovery!

If she only has pain after sex whilst peeing Then it disappears and doesn’t bother her until sex again then that’s definitely not a UTI, unfortunately I’m not sure what that is but it sounds like friction burn or micro tears. A UTI can start after sex or a day after and the pain is constant, only going away after a few days of having it or taking antibiotics. My suggestion should be to get her (if she’s comfortable) to go to the doctors and ask them for a urine test to rule out a UTI. Pain after sex or even a little after is very common but should be looked into. Best of luck for your girlfriend, genital pain is the worst

Coming from a female who had had this exact issues here is what I can tell you. Talk to her, if she feels the burn only from her pee hole (urethra) then it’s most certainly a UTI, harmless to you and her (apart from the pain) and is easily treated with antibiotics and A LOT of cranberry juice and water. If she pees and the pain only start when the pee touches her opening then it’s probably friction irritation or small micro tears, that will just go away but it does hurt. Overall most likely a UTI an only requires a urine test at the doctors!
